# 1 Enoch Chapter 71 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** And it came to pass after this that my spirit was translated and ascended into the heavens; and I saw the holy sons of God. They were stepping on flames of fire; their garments were white, and their faces shone like snow.

**2** And I saw two streams of fire, and the light of that fire shone like hyacinth, and I fell on my face before the Lord of Spirits.

**3** And the angel Michael, one of the archangels, seized me by my right hand and lifted me up and led me forth into all the secrets, and he showed me all the secrets of righteousness.

**4** And he showed me all the secrets of the ends of heaven, and all the chambers of all the stars, and all the luminaries, from where they proceed before the face of the holy ones.

**5** And he translated my spirit, even Enoch, to the heaven of heavens, and I saw there as it were a structure built of crystals, and between those crystals tongues of living fire.

**6** And my spirit saw the girdle which girt that house of fire, and on its four sides were streams full of living fire, and they girt that house.

**7** And round about were Seraphim, Cherubim, and Ophanim; and these are they who sleep not and guard the throne of his glory.

**8** And I saw angels who could not be counted — a thousand thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand — encircling that house. And Michael, and Raphael, and Gabriel, and Phanuel, and the holy angels who are above the heavens, go in and out of that house.

**9** And they came forth from that house — Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, and many holy angels without number.

**10** And with them the Head of Days, his head white and pure as wool, and his raiment indescribable.

**11** And I fell on my face, and my whole body became relaxed, and my spirit was transfigured; and I cried with a loud voice, with the spirit of power, and blessed and glorified and extolled.

**12** And these blessings which went forth from my mouth were well pleasing before that Head of Days.

**13** And that Head of Days came with Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel, and thousands and ten thousands of angels without number.

**14** And he came to me and greeted me with his voice, and said to me: You are that Son of Man who was born unto righteousness, and righteousness abides over you, and the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes you not.

**15** And he said to me: He proclaims to you peace in the name of the world to come; for from there peace has gone forth since the creation of the world, and so shall it be unto you for ever and ever and unto all eternity.

**16** And all shall walk in his ways, since righteousness never forsakes him; with him will be their dwelling-places, and with him their heritage, and they shall not be separated from him for ever and ever and unto all eternity.

**17** And so there shall be length of days with that Son of Man, and the righteous shall have peace and an upright way in the name of the Lord of Spirits for ever and ever.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering.*

*CRITICAL NOTE — 71:14: The most debated verse in Second Temple literature. Two main MS traditions diverge here:*

*(A) MAJORITY READING (adopted by LOGOS): "You are that Son of Man who was born unto righteousness." In this reading, the Head of Days (or his representative) speaks directly to Enoch, identifying Enoch himself as the Son of Man. This is the identification reading — Enoch = the Son of Man.*

*(B) MINORITY/VARIANT READING: "This is the Son of Man who was born unto righteousness" — in which the speaker presents a third figure (the Son of Man) to Enoch.*

*LOGOS adopts the majority reading ("You are that Son of Man") on the grounds that: (1) it has stronger MS support; (2) ch. 70:1 already suggested that Enoch's name was 'raised aloft to the Son of Man' — the identification is being completed; (3) the address is in second person throughout vv. 14-16 ('you...you'), making a third-person presentation awkward.*

*The phrase 'born unto righteousness' (Ge'ez za-wald la-sedeq) is itself debated: does it describe Enoch's birth (making him a human being who was exalted) or an eternal generation? LOGOS preserves the literal 'born unto righteousness' without resolving this.*
